frames.narration: Directory v8 assigns three disjoint hash ranges to S1, S2, and S3.
frames.outcome: Every hash has one active owner.
frames.invariant: Ranges cover the keyspace exactly once within an epoch.

frames.title: Route hash 62
frames.narration: The partition index finds range [50,74] and returns S2.
frames.outcome: The request reaches one shard instead of broadcasting.
frames.invariant: Clients route using one internally consistent directory epoch.

frames.title: Start online copy
frames.narration: S4 receives a snapshot of S2's range while v8 still routes reads and writes to S2.
frames.outcome: Foreground ownership remains stable during bulk movement.
frames.invariant: A shadow copy cannot serve authoritative writes before cutover.

frames.title: Catch up and cut over
frames.narration: After S4 replays through LSN 944, directory v9 changes [50,74] to S4.
frames.outcome: New requests route to S4.
frames.invariant: An epoch change atomically selects one write owner per range.

frames.title: Reject stale routing
frames.narration: A v8 client sent to S2 receives epoch 9 and retries against S4.
frames.outcome: The moved range has no split write authority.
frames.invariant: Owners reject requests carrying an obsolete routing epoch.

storage-systems::Columnar storage.title: Columnar storage
storage-systems::Columnar storage.summary: Columnar storage keeps values by column, enabling compression and scans over selected fields.
storage-systems::Columnar storage.tradeoff: Point updates and full-row reconstruction are comparatively expensive.

mechanism.scenario: An analytical scan reads only region and revenue columns from compressed row groups.

frames.title: Group values by column
frames.narration: One row group stores each field contiguously instead of storing complete rows together.
frames.outcome: Similar values share pages and compression context.
frames.invariant: All columns preserve the same row-position ordering.

frames.title: Prune unused columns
frames.narration: The projection and predicate require only region and revenue; id and name pages stay unread.
frames.outcome: Three quarters of the logical fields are initially skipped.
frames.invariant: Column pruning must retain every predicate and output dependency.

frames.title: Build a selection vector
frames.narration: Scanning the region column marks row positions 0 and 2 as EU.
frames.outcome: The selection vector avoids materializing nonmatching rows.
frames.invariant: A position refers to the same logical row across every column.

frames.title: Read selected measures
frames.narration: The revenue page contributes values 8 and 7 at selected positions.
frames.outcome: The aggregate equals 15 without reading names or IDs.
frames.invariant: Aggregation consumes only values selected by the predicate vector.

frames.title: Contrast row reconstruction
frames.narration: A point request for row 3 must gather position 2 from all four columns.
frames.outcome: Columnar analytics are efficient while full-row reconstruction touches more pages.
frames.invariant: A reconstructed row uses one identical ordinal from every required column.

storage-systems::Row-oriented storage.title: Row-oriented storage
storage-systems::Row-oriented storage.summary: Row-oriented storage co-locates all fields of a record for efficient point reads and writes.
storage-systems::Row-oriented storage.tradeoff: Analytical scans read unnecessary columns and compress less effectively.

mechanism.scenario: An OLTP heap co-locates each customer's fields so a primary-key point read and update touch one row page.

frames.title: Co-locate complete rows
frames.narration: Page P7 stores each customer's ID, name, region, and revenue together by row slot.
frames.outcome: A complete tuple occupies one contiguous record.
frames.invariant: Each slot is independently addressable within its page.

frames.title: Resolve row location
frames.narration: The primary directory maps ID 42 to P7 slot 1.
frames.outcome: Only page P7 must be fetched.
frames.invariant: The directory pointer identifies one current row slot.

frames.title: Read the complete tuple
frames.narration: One slot read returns 42, Ada, EU, and revenue 8.
frames.outcome: The point query needs no cross-page reconstruction.
frames.invariant: All fields in a row share one record version.

frames.title: Update one field in place
frames.narration: Revenue changes from 8 to 10 inside row 42 and marks P7 dirty.
frames.outcome: The updated tuple remains co-located.
frames.invariant: A row update publishes one consistent record image.

frames.title: Expose analytical cost
frames.narration: SUM(revenue) scans revenue fields embedded in all three row records.
frames.outcome: The aggregate reads unrelated name and region bytes from the same page.
frames.invariant: Row layout optimizes tuple locality, not single-column scans.

storage-systems::Log-structured storage.title: Log-structured storage
storage-systems::Log-structured storage.summary: Log-structured storage appends new versions sequentially and reorganizes data asynchronously.
storage-systems::Log-structured storage.tradeoff: Requires garbage collection or compaction and indirect reads.

mechanism.scenario: A key-value store appends new versions, resolves reads through a location index, and cleans segments by copying live records.

frames.title: Start with sealed records
frames.narration: S1 contains a=1 and b=2; the location index points both keys into S1.
frames.outcome: Reads find current records indirectly through the index.
frames.invariant: A location index points to the newest appended version.

frames.title: Append a new version
frames.narration: PUT b=9 writes a complete record at the S3 tail rather than overwriting S1.
frames.outcome: The old b=2 becomes reclaimable dead data.
frames.invariant: Foreground writes advance the append tail monotonically.

frames.title: Publish the new location
frames.narration: The index atomically changes b from S1:1 to S3:0.
frames.outcome: Reads of b now return 9.
frames.invariant: Index publication follows durable append and exposes only a complete record.

frames.title: Select a dirty segment
frames.narration: Cleaner chooses S1 because half its records are dead and copies only live a=1 to S4.
frames.outcome: Dead b=2 is omitted from cleaner output.
frames.invariant: Cleaning copies a record only if the index still names its old location.

frames.title: Swap locations and reclaim
frames.narration: The index moves a to S4:0, then S1 is deleted.

action.label: publish a S4:0 and retire S1

frames.outcome: Space is reclaimed without blocking append-only writes.
frames.invariant: A segment is removed only after every live copied record has a published new location.

storage-systems::Object storage.title: Object storage
storage-systems::Object storage.summary: Object storage addresses whole blobs by key with metadata and massive namespace scale.
storage-systems::Object storage.tradeoff: Higher latency and whole-object operations make random mutation inefficient.

mechanism.scenario: An object store resolves a key to immutable metadata and a version manifest whose chunks are distributed across storage nodes.

frames.title: Resolve immutable metadata
frames.narration: The key maps to version 17, content length 9 MiB, checksum 71de, and manifest m17.
frames.outcome: Namespace metadata describes one immutable object version.
frames.invariant: A version's length, checksum, and manifest pointer do not mutate.

frames.title: Load the manifest
frames.narration: Manifest m17 orders chunk hashes a8f, b31, and c09 with exact lengths.
frames.outcome: The reader knows which byte ranges to fetch.
frames.invariant: Manifest order defines object byte order.

frames.title: Fetch chunks in parallel
frames.narration: The client requests all three content-addressed chunks from their storage nodes.
frames.outcome: Nine MiB of chunk payload is available for assembly.
frames.invariant: Each returned chunk must match its manifest hash.

frames.title: Verify and assemble
frames.narration: Hashes verify all chunks before concatenation in manifest order.
frames.outcome: The complete cat.jpg bytes are returned.
frames.invariant: Assembly never mixes chunks from different manifests.

frames.title: Publish a replacement version
frames.narration: A PUT creates manifest m18 and atomically advances only the key's metadata pointer.
frames.outcome: Readers choose either complete v17 or complete v18.
frames.invariant: Object replacement publishes a new immutable version rather than patching chunks in place.

storage-systems::Block storage.title: Block storage
storage-systems::Block storage.summary: Block storage exposes low-level fixed-size blocks for filesystems and databases.
storage-systems::Block storage.tradeoff: Shared access and higher-level consistency must be built above it.

mechanism.scenario: A virtual disk controller maps logical blocks to mirrored physical extents and repairs a failed replica.

frames.title: Map the logical block
frames.narration: Volume v3 maps LBA 12 to mirrored extent E7 on nodes A and B.
frames.outcome: The host sees a stable block number independent of physical placement.
frames.invariant: One mapping generation identifies the authoritative replica set.

frames.title: Issue a block write
frames.narration: The host sends 4 KiB payload checksum 9c1 to the controller for LBA 12.
frames.outcome: The controller fans the write to both extents.
frames.invariant: Replicas receive identical block generation and checksum.

frames.title: Acknowledge durable mirrors
frames.narration: Nodes A and B fsync generation 44 and return acknowledgements.
frames.outcome: The controller safely acknowledges the host write.
frames.invariant: Success requires the configured number of durable replica acknowledgements.

frames.title: Detect one failed extent
frames.narration: Node B stops responding; reads continue from A while C is allocated as a repair target.
frames.outcome: The volume remains readable but degraded.
frames.invariant: Repair copies from a replica whose generation and checksum are current.

frames.title: Complete repair and remap
frames.narration: C verifies checksum 9c1, then mapping generation 5 replaces B with C.
frames.outcome: The block returns to two healthy copies.
frames.invariant: A replacement joins the active map only after complete verified synchronization.

storage-systems::Distributed filesystems.title: Distributed filesystems
storage-systems::Distributed filesystems.summary: Distributed filesystems provide shared file semantics across replicated storage nodes.
storage-systems::Distributed filesystems.tradeoff: Metadata coordination, small files, and cross-node consistency can bottleneck scale.

mechanism.scenario: A distributed filesystem resolves a pathname through namespace metadata, reads replicated chunks, and repairs a lost copy.

frames.title: Resolve the namespace
frames.narration: The metadata authority maps /logs/app to file ID f81 and generation 12.
frames.outcome: The hierarchical name resolves independently of data placement.
frames.invariant: One namespace generation identifies the current file manifest.

frames.title: Load chunk metadata
frames.narration: File f81 consists of ordered chunks C10 and C11 with replication factor two.
frames.outcome: The client receives chunk order and replica locations.
frames.invariant: Every published chunk has the configured number of distinct hosts.

frames.title: Read nearby replicas
frames.narration: The client reads C10 from A and C11 from C and concatenates them by chunk ordinal.

action.label: read C10 from A and C11 from C

frames.outcome: The file stream is reconstructed without routing data through the namespace authority.
frames.invariant: Chunk bytes are ordered by the file manifest, not response time.

frames.title: Detect under-replication
frames.narration: Server B fails, leaving C10 only on A and C11 only on C.
frames.outcome: Metadata marks both chunks under-replicated and chooses nonfailed targets.
frames.invariant: Failure detection changes placement metadata only after a host lease expires.

frames.title: Repair and publish locations
frames.narration: A copies C10 to C, C copies C11 to A, and verified replicas restore factor two.
frames.outcome: The file is healthy despite losing one chunk server.
frames.invariant: New locations publish only after chunk identity and checksum verification.

database-distributed-system-concepts::Co.title: Consistent hashing
database-distributed-system-concepts::Co.summary: Consistent hashing maps keys to owners while minimizing movement when membership changes.
database-distributed-system-concepts::Co.tradeoff: It loses range locality and still needs virtual nodes or weighting for balance.

mechanism.scenario: A cache cluster moves a small key range when node N3 joins the ring.

frames.title: Place initial nodes
frames.narration: N1@10, N2@40, and N4@90 partition the hash ring.
frames.outcome: Three clockwise ownership ranges exist.
frames.invariant: A key belongs to the first node token at or after its hash, wrapping at 100.

frames.title: Assign keys clockwise
frames.narration: alpha@35 maps to N2, while beta@65 and gamma@85 map to N4.
frames.outcome: Every key has one primary successor.
frames.invariant: Ownership ranges are open on the predecessor and closed on the owner.

frames.title: Join N3 at token 70
frames.narration: N3 inserts between N2 and N4 and takes responsibility for hashes (40,70].
frames.outcome: Only beta moves to the joining node.
frames.invariant: A join changes ownership only in the new node's predecessor range.

frames.title: Add clockwise replicas
frames.narration: Replication factor two stores each key on its primary and next distinct node.
frames.outcome: Each key survives one node failure.
frames.invariant: Replica owners are the next distinct clockwise nodes.

frames.title: Route a lookup
frames.narration: A lookup for beta@65 walks clockwise to N3 and reads its primary copy.
frames.outcome: The coordinator deterministically selects N3.
frames.invariant: All clients using the same ring view compute the same owner.

database-distributed-system-concepts::Qu.title: Quorum
database-distributed-system-concepts::Qu.summary: A quorum is an intersecting subset of replicas used to make or observe authoritative decisions.

frames.title: Replica set
frames.narration: N=3 replicas hold profile x; R1 and R2 have v4 while lagging R3 has v3.
frames.outcome: A majority contains the latest acknowledged version.
frames.invariant: R+W>N gives read/write quorum overlap.

frames.title: Read two replicas
frames.narration: The coordinator requests R1 and R3 and receives versions v4 and v3.
frames.outcome: The highest version v4 wins.
frames.invariant: A quorum read compares version metadata, not response arrival order.

frames.title: Repair stale replica
frames.narration: Read repair sends v4 blue to R3 after returning the selected value.
frames.outcome: All replicas converge to v4.
frames.invariant: Repair never replaces a higher version with a lower one.

frames.title: Write version five
frames.narration: The client writes red at v5; R1 and R2 acknowledge while R3 is temporarily unavailable.
frames.outcome: W=2 acknowledges the write despite one failed replica.
frames.invariant: A write succeeds only after W distinct acknowledgements.

frames.title: Read after write
frames.narration: A later quorum read from R2 and R3 sees v5 and v4, returns red, and schedules R3 repair.
frames.outcome: The acknowledged write is visible through quorum overlap.
frames.invariant: With R+W>N, every read quorum intersects the successful write quorum.

streaming-real-time-processing::Watermar.summary: Watermarks estimate how complete event-time progress is across input partitions.

mechanism.scenario: Two partitions report event-time progress despite out-of-order arrivals.

frames.title: Observe partition zero
frames.narration: P0 sees event time 100; five seconds of allowed disorder gives candidate 95.
frames.outcome: Global progress waits for P1.
frames.invariant: A watermark cannot exceed any active partition's candidate.

frames.title: Observe partition one
frames.narration: P1 sees time 98, producing candidate 93 and global watermark 93.
frames.outcome: Event times through 93 are considered complete.
frames.invariant: The global watermark is the minimum active candidate.

frames.title: Accept out of order
frames.narration: P0 receives time 97 after 100; it is newer than watermark 93 and remains on time.
frames.outcome: Out-of-order does not automatically mean late.
frames.invariant: Partition maxima and watermarks never move backward.

frames.title: Advance both partitions
frames.narration: P0 reaches 105 and P1 reaches 101, moving the global watermark to 96.
frames.outcome: Windows ending at or before 96 may close.
frames.invariant: Global event-time progress is monotonic.

frames.title: Classify a late event
frames.narration: An event at time 94 arrives behind watermark 96 and follows the late-data policy.
frames.outcome: The record is routed to late handling.
frames.invariant: An event is late when event time is less than the current watermark.

frames.narration: DFS uses a stack and follows A-B-D-F before backtracking.

frames.title: Backtrack and finish
frames.narration: DFS pops to B, explores E, then returns to A for C.
frames.outcome: All reachable nodes are visited in depth-first order.
frames.invariant: Every non-root node has one DFS-tree parent.

distributed-algorithms::Dijkstra.title: Dijkstra
distributed-algorithms::Dijkstra.summary: Dijkstra finds shortest paths from a source when edge weights are nonnegative.
distributed-algorithms::Dijkstra.tradeoff: Priority-queue coordination is costly to parallelize and negative edges are unsupported.

mechanism.scenario: A router computes nonnegative shortest paths from A.

frames.title: Initialize distances
frames.narration: A starts at zero; all other distances are infinity.
frames.outcome: The source is the only frontier node.
frames.invariant: Unreached vertices have infinite tentative distance.

frames.title: Settle A
frames.narration: Relaxing A→B and A→C yields distances 2 and 5.
frames.outcome: B becomes the nearest tentative node.
frames.invariant: Relaxation uses dist[u]+nonnegative edge weight.

frames.title: Settle B
frames.narration: B improves D to 3 and E to 6.
frames.outcome: D moves ahead of C in the priority queue.
frames.invariant: A settled vertex never needs a smaller distance.

frames.title: Settle D then C
frames.narration: D gives F=6; C improves E from 6 to 6 via an equal path, retaining the first parent.
frames.outcome: All remaining tentative distances are six.
frames.invariant: Priority order is by smallest tentative distance.

frames.title: Finish shortest paths
frames.narration: Settling E and F completes distances and parent paths.
frames.outcome: Shortest route to F is A-B-D-F with cost 6.
frames.invariant: Every settled distance is final because all edge weights are nonnegative.

distributed-algorithms::Bellman-Ford.title: Bellman-Ford
distributed-algorithms::Bellman-Ford.summary: Bellman-Ford repeatedly relaxes edges and supports negative weights while detecting negative cycles.
distributed-algorithms::Bellman-Ford.tradeoff: More general but much slower than Dijkstra on large graphs.

mechanism.scenario: A routing table handles a negative edge and detects negative cycles.

frames.title: Initialize source
frames.narration: A is zero and all other distances are infinity.
frames.outcome: Only A is reachable initially.
frames.invariant: Distances are upper bounds on shortest paths.

frames.title: First full pass
frames.narration: Relaxing every edge yields B=4, C=2 through B, D=5, E=4.
frames.outcome: Paths using several edges propagate within the pass order.
frames.invariant: Each relaxation only lowers a distance.

frames.title: Second pass stable
frames.narration: A second pass finds no shorter candidate.
frames.outcome: The solution converges early.
frames.invariant: No update means all edge inequalities hold.

frames.title: Verify remaining passes
frames.narration: Passes three and four remain unchanged for five vertices.
frames.outcome: Shortest distances are final.
frames.invariant: At most |V|-1 edges are needed by any simple shortest path.

frames.title: Negative-cycle check
frames.narration: A final edge scan cannot lower any distance, proving no reachable negative cycle.
frames.outcome: Routes are safe to publish.
frames.invariant: Any update on pass |V| would prove a reachable negative cycle.

distributed-algorithms::Minimum spanning.title: Minimum spanning tree
distributed-algorithms::Minimum spanning.summary: A minimum spanning tree connects all vertices with minimum total edge weight and no cycles.
distributed-algorithms::Minimum spanning.tradeoff: Models connectivity cost, not shortest routes from a source.

mechanism.scenario: Prim's algorithm grows a minimum spanning tree by repeatedly selecting the cheapest edge crossing from the tree to an outside vertex.

frames.title: Seed the tree at A
frames.narration: A enters the tree and exposes AB=1 and AC=4 to the frontier.
frames.outcome: AB is the minimum crossing edge.
frames.invariant: Every frontier edge has exactly one endpoint in the current tree when inserted.

frames.title: Select AB
frames.narration: AB=1 adds B and exposes BC=2 and BD=5.
frames.outcome: C's best attachment improves from AC=4 to BC=2.
frames.invariant: Selecting an edge adds exactly one previously outside vertex.

frames.title: Select BC
frames.narration: BC=2 adds C; CD=1 and CE=3 enter the heap while stale AC=4 remains removable.
frames.outcome: CD becomes the cheapest edge across the cut.
frames.invariant: For each outside vertex, its key is the cheapest discovered connection to the tree.

frames.title: Discard an internal edge
frames.narration: AC=4 now has both endpoints in the tree, so lazy heap cleanup rejects it without changing the MST.
frames.outcome: The frontier again contains only useful crossing candidates.
frames.invariant: An edge whose outside endpoint already joined cannot be selected.

frames.title: Select CD then DE
frames.narration: CD=1 adds D, which exposes DE=2; DE then beats CE=3 and adds E.
frames.outcome: Four edges span all five vertices at total weight six.
frames.invariant: The selected edge is the lightest edge crossing the current cut.

frames.title: Finalize the spanning tree
frames.narration: Remaining CE=3 and BD=5 are internal edges and are rejected.
frames.outcome: The result is connected, acyclic, and has minimum total weight.
frames.invariant: A spanning tree over five vertices contains exactly four selected edges.

distributed-algorithms::Kruskal.title: Kruskal
distributed-algorithms::Kruskal.summary: Kruskal adds edges in weight order when they connect different components.
distributed-algorithms::Kruskal.tradeoff: Requires global edge ordering but parallel component checks can help.

mechanism.scenario: A network planner builds a minimum spanning tree by globally sorted links.

frames.title: Sort all edges
frames.narration: Edges order as AB1, CD1, BC2, DF2, CE3, AC4, EF4, BD5.
frames.outcome: Cheapest links will be considered first.
frames.invariant: Edge order is nondecreasing by weight.

frames.title: Select weight-one edges
frames.narration: AB and CD join disjoint components.
frames.outcome: Four components remain.
frames.invariant: Selected edges never connect vertices already in one component.

frames.title: Join with weight two
frames.narration: BC merges AB with CD; DF adds F to that component.
frames.outcome: Only E remains separate.
frames.invariant: Union operations merge entire components.

frames.title: Add final component
frames.narration: CE with weight 3 joins E and completes five selected edges.
frames.outcome: The spanning tree is complete at total weight 9.
frames.invariant: A tree on six vertices has exactly five selected edges.

frames.title: Reject cycle edges
frames.narration: Remaining AC, EF, and BD connect vertices already unified and are rejected.
frames.outcome: No selected edge creates a cycle.
frames.invariant: Kruskal accepts an edge iff its endpoints are in different components.

distributed-algorithms::Prim.title: Prim
distributed-algorithms::Prim.summary: Prim grows one tree by repeatedly adding the cheapest edge leaving it.
distributed-algorithms::Prim.tradeoff: Efficient on dense graphs but frontier coordination can bottleneck distribution.

mechanism.scenario: A network planner grows a minimum spanning tree outward from A.

frames.title: Seed vertex A
frames.narration: A enters the tree and exposes AB1 and AC4.
frames.outcome: AB is the cheapest crossing edge.
frames.invariant: The frontier contains only edges with one endpoint in the tree.

frames.title: Attach B
frames.narration: AB1 adds B and introduces BC2 and BD5.
frames.outcome: C's best connection improves from four to two.
frames.invariant: Each outside vertex tracks its cheapest crossing edge.

frames.title: Attach C
frames.narration: BC2 adds C; CD1 becomes the cheapest frontier edge and CE3 appears.
frames.outcome: D now has key one.
frames.invariant: Keys decrease when a cheaper crossing edge is discovered.

frames.title: Attach D and F
frames.narration: CD1 adds D, then DF2 adds F.
frames.outcome: Only E remains outside.
frames.invariant: Each selected edge adds exactly one new vertex.

frames.title: Attach E
frames.narration: CE3 beats FE4 and completes the tree at weight 9.
frames.outcome: All vertices are connected by a minimum spanning tree.
frames.invariant: The chosen edge is always the lightest edge crossing the current cut.

distributed-algorithms::Topological sort.title: Topological sort
distributed-algorithms::Topological sort.summary: Topological sort orders a directed acyclic graph so every dependency precedes its dependents.
distributed-algorithms::Topological sort.tradeoff: Cycles make the ordering impossible and must be detected.

mechanism.scenario: A deployment scheduler orders services subject to directed dependencies.

frames.title: Count indegrees
frames.narration: A and B have zero prerequisites; C has two, D one, E two, F one.
frames.outcome: The ready queue contains A and B.
frames.invariant: Indegree equals the number of unremoved incoming edges.

frames.title: Schedule A
frames.narration: Removing A emits it and decrements C from two to one.
frames.outcome: C still waits for B.
frames.invariant: Only zero-indegree nodes may be emitted.

frames.title: Schedule B
frames.narration: Removing B makes C and D ready.
frames.outcome: Both immediate dependents can now run.
frames.invariant: Removing a node decrements each outgoing neighbor once.

frames.title: Schedule C and D
frames.narration: C then D remove both incoming edges to E, making E ready.
frames.outcome: E is released only after both prerequisites.
frames.invariant: Every emitted prefix respects all edges within the prefix.

frames.title: Finish E then F
frames.narration: E releases F; all six nodes are emitted without a cycle.
frames.outcome: A valid deployment order is A,B,C,D,E,F.
frames.invariant: For every directed edge u→v, u appears before v.

distributed-algorithms::Union-Find.title: Union-Find
distributed-algorithms::Union-Find.summary: Union-Find maintains disjoint sets with near-constant-time union and connectivity checks.
distributed-algorithms::Union-Find.tradeoff: Excellent for incremental merges but not deletions or rich component queries.

mechanism.scenario: A connectivity service incrementally groups hosts and answers reachability.

frames.title: Singleton sets
frames.narration: Every host begins as its own parent with rank zero.
frames.outcome: Six disjoint components exist.
frames.invariant: A root is a node whose parent is itself.

frames.title: Union A and B
frames.narration: Equal ranks choose A as root and raise A's rank to one.
frames.outcome: A and B share root A.
frames.invariant: Union decreases component count only for distinct roots.

frames.title: Build two components
frames.narration: Union B-C attaches C under A; union D-E chooses D as root.
frames.outcome: Components are ABC, DE, and F.
frames.invariant: Trees represent sets without changing member identity.

frames.title: Union by rank
frames.narration: Union C-D joins equal-rank roots A and D; D becomes child of A and A rank becomes two.
frames.outcome: ABCDE now form one component.
frames.invariant: The lower-rank root attaches below the higher-rank root; ties raise one rank.

frames.title: Compress find path
frames.narration: find(E) follows E→D→A and rewrites E directly to A.
frames.outcome: Future finds for E take one hop.
frames.invariant: Path compression changes parents but never component membership.

distributed-algorithms::Consistent hashi.title: Consistent hashing
distributed-algorithms::Consistent hashi.summary: Consistent hashing assigns keys to changing members while minimizing remapping.
distributed-algorithms::Consistent hashi.tradeoff: Needs balancing techniques and provides no range locality.

mechanism.scenario: A partition router adds node N3 to a versioned hash ring and migrates only the newly owned clockwise range.

frames.title: Publish the initial ring
frames.narration: Epoch 11 contains N1@10, N2@40, and N4@90; ranges wrap clockwise.
frames.outcome: Each hash position has exactly one primary clockwise successor.
frames.invariant: All routers use an immutable ring epoch for a request.

frames.title: Route existing keys
frames.narration: alpha@35 resolves to N2 and beta@65 resolves to N4 under epoch 11.
frames.outcome: Routing requires one hash and a clockwise token lookup.
frames.invariant: The owner is the first token greater than or equal to the key hash, with wraparound.

frames.title: Insert joining token
frames.narration: The controller prepares epoch 12 with N3@70 between N2 and N4.
frames.outcome: Only N4's former subrange (40,70] changes ownership in the staged ring.
frames.invariant: The active epoch does not change before required range data is copied.

frames.title: Stream the affected range
frames.narration: The mover copies beta@65 and its version while writes in (40,70] are dual-recorded to N4 and N3.

action.label: copy beta and catch up range log

frames.outcome: N3 has a complete copy through the cutover log position.
frames.invariant: Migration copies only keys whose hashes fall in the joining node's predecessor range.

frames.title: Atomically publish epoch 12
frames.narration: Routers switch to epoch 12, making N3 primary for beta while alpha remains on N2.
frames.outcome: Only beta changes primary owner, and replica successors are recomputed.
frames.invariant: A request routes entirely with either epoch 11 or epoch 12, never a mixed view.

frames.title: Retire the old primary copy
frames.narration: After epoch-11 requests drain, N4 retains beta only as N3's clockwise replica and range migration completes.
frames.outcome: The ring is balanced without moving alpha or unrelated ranges.
frames.invariant: Old ownership is removed only after new ownership is durable and old-epoch traffic has drained.

distributed-algorithms::Leader election.title: Leader election
distributed-algorithms::Leader election.summary: Leader election chooses one authority for an epoch among distributed participants.
distributed-algorithms::Leader election.tradeoff: Partitions and pauses require quorum rules and fencing of stale leaders.

mechanism.scenario: Three Raft replicas elect N2 in term 8, establish authority with heartbeats, and step down on a higher term.

frames.title: Followers await heartbeats
frames.narration: All replicas are followers in term 7; N2 has the earliest randomized election deadline.
frames.outcome: No leader is known after the previous heartbeat lease expires.
frames.invariant: A replica grants at most one vote per term.

frames.title: N2 starts term eight
frames.narration: At 180 ms N2 increments its term, votes for itself, and requests votes with lastLog=(12,7).
frames.outcome: N2 is a candidate with one self-vote.
frames.invariant: Election requests carry the candidate term and last-log position.

frames.title: Followers evaluate the candidate
frames.narration: N1 and N3 update to term 8; N2's log is at least as up-to-date, so both grant their term-8 vote.
frames.outcome: N2 has three votes, exceeding the two-node majority.
frames.invariant: A vote is granted only once per term and only to a candidate with an up-to-date log.

frames.title: Become leader and assert authority
frames.narration: N2 becomes leader and immediately sends empty AppendEntries heartbeats carrying term 8 and prevLogIndex 12.
frames.outcome: Followers reset their timers and clients can discover N2.
frames.invariant: Leadership is valid only within the elected term and maintained by periodic AppendEntries.

frames.title: Replicate a leader entry
frames.narration: N2 appends command x at index 13 term 8 and commits after N1 acknowledges, a majority of two.

action.label: append x at index 13 and replicate

frames.outcome: Command x is committed despite N3 lagging.
frames.invariant: Only the current leader advances commit after a majority stores the entry.

frames.title: Step down on a higher term
frames.narration: N3 later presents term 9; N2 updates its term, clears leadership, and rejects leader-only client writes.
frames.outcome: No term-8 leader continues accepting writes.
frames.invariant: Any message with a higher term immediately invalidates lower-term candidacy or leadership.

distributed-algorithms::Distributed snap.summary: A distributed snapshot captures a causally consistent global state without stopping all participants.
distributed-algorithms::Distributed snap.tradeoff: In-flight messages and channel recording add protocol and storage cost.

mechanism.scenario: Three processes run Chandy-Lamport over FIFO channels and capture a consistent snapshot containing one in-flight transfer.

frames.title: Place a transfer in C12
frames.narration: Before snapshot S1, P1 sends m12=$2: P1 falls from 5 to 3 while the undelivered message sits in C12.
frames.outcome: Money is conserved across process balances and channel contents.
frames.invariant: A send atomically debits the sender before the FIFO message enters its channel.

frames.title: P1 initiates snapshot S1
frames.narration: P1 records local balance 3, starts recording incoming C31, and appends marker S1 after m12 on outgoing C12.

action.label: record P1=3 and send marker S1

frames.outcome: P1's local cut is fixed while its incoming channel remains open.
frames.invariant: An initiator records local state before sending a marker on every outgoing channel.

frames.title: P2 receives data before the marker
frames.narration: FIFO delivery applies m12 first, raising P2 from 4 to 6; the following marker then records P2=6 and an empty C12 snapshot.
frames.outcome: P2's snapshot includes the transfer in local state, not in C12.
frames.invariant: On the first marker, a process records local state and treats that incoming channel as empty.

frames.title: Create an in-flight C31 transfer
frames.narration: After P1's cut but before P3's cut, P3 sends m31=$1; P3 falls to 5 and P1 records the arriving message on open channel C31.
frames.outcome: P1 applies m31 to live balance 4 but keeps snapshot-local balance 3.
frames.invariant: Messages arriving on an open incoming channel are recorded until that channel's marker arrives.

frames.title: P3 receives its first marker
frames.narration: Marker S1 on C23 makes P3 record local balance 5, mark C23 empty, and send its marker on C31 after m31.

action.label: record P3=5 and send marker on C31

frames.outcome: All three local states are now captured.
frames.invariant: FIFO ordering places P3's marker after every earlier message it sent on C31.

frames.title: Close P1's incoming channel
frames.narration: P1 receives the C31 marker and stops recording; C31's snapshot contains exactly m31=$1.

action.label: receive marker and close C31 recording

frames.outcome: Every process has received a marker on every incoming channel.
frames.invariant: A channel snapshot contains messages sent before the sender's cut and received after the receiver's cut.

frames.title: Assemble the global snapshot
frames.narration: The collector combines local balances 3+6+5 with C31's in-flight $1 for a conserved total of $15.

action.label: publish locals and channel records for S1

frames.outcome: S1 is a consistent global cut even though live execution never stopped.
frames.invariant: Local snapshot value plus recorded channel value preserves the system-wide conservation invariant.

distributed-algorithms::Distributed aggr.title: Distributed aggregation
distributed-algorithms::Distributed aggr.summary: Distributed aggregation merges partition-local summaries into a global result.

mechanism.scenario: A binary aggregation tree computes a cluster-wide sum with sequence-numbered partials, then broadcasts the result to every leaf.

frames.title: Open aggregation round 27
frames.narration: Four leaves freeze local contributions W0=3, W1=5, W2=4, and W3=8 under sequence 27.
frames.outcome: Every leaf has one immutable contribution for this round.
frames.invariant: A worker contributes at most once for an aggregation sequence.

frames.title: Send leaf partials upward
frames.narration: W0 and W1 send to A0; W2 and W3 send to A1 with sender IDs and sequence 27.
frames.outcome: Both internal aggregators have their complete child sets.
frames.invariant: A receiver keys partials by sequence and child ID to make retries idempotent.

frames.title: Ignore a duplicate retry
frames.narration: A delayed retry of W1=5 is recognized as the same sequence-child pair and does not change A0.
frames.outcome: A0 still represents exactly two leaves.
frames.invariant: Duplicate delivery cannot alter an aggregation round.

frames.title: Reduce each subtree
frames.narration: A0 emits 3+5=8 and A1 emits 4+8=12 to the root.
frames.outcome: Two subtree partials replace four leaf messages at the root.
frames.invariant: Each internal subtotal equals the sum of its disjoint descendant leaves.

frames.title: Compute the global aggregate
frames.narration: R waits for both configured children, then commits global sum 20 for sequence 27.
frames.outcome: The tree root has the exact cluster-wide sum.
frames.invariant: The root finalizes only after one partial from every expected child subtree.

frames.title: Broadcast the all-reduce result
frames.narration: The committed value flows down the tree until all four workers install result 20 for round 27.
frames.outcome: Every participant observes the same aggregate without all-to-all traffic.
frames.invariant: A worker installs a result only when its sequence matches the active aggregation round.
